## Original Instrumental Soundtrack with Editable Strudel Source and WAV Master

- Identity: `fraylabs/possible/original-strudel-soundtrack`
- Slug: `original-strudel-soundtrack`
- Status: `experimental`
- Pack version: `1.0.0`
- Public page: https://possible.sh/packs/original-strudel-soundtrack/
- Origin: `bundled`
- Source: package:@possible/packs
- Revision: `pack:1.0.0`
- Manifest path: `manifests/original-strudel-soundtrack.json`
- Content hash: `sha256:e968a2c749bd34c151ff3b95a84cfea599ed640bedaf98dceb455ab5d79b9d4f`
- Accepted snapshot: `manifests/original-strudel-soundtrack.json`
- Accepted evidence: none
- Promise: Compose one complete original soundtrack in the official Strudel runtime and deliver editable Strudel source, an official WAV export, a listening master, and evidence that the music works technically and for its intended listener.
- Summary: A music-first contract for turning a mood, reference, scene, product, game, or other listening context into an original instrumental soundtrack with a deliberate musical identity and arc. The agent studies reference qualities without copying them, composes a complete piece rather than a decorated loop, then clones the official Codeberg Strudel repository at the pack's reviewed revision and uses that local application to play and export the result. Metrics can expose silence, clipping, harshness, or a flat dynamic profile, but they never substitute for listening: the outcome passes only when a human reviewer has heard the actual master and accepts its musical fit. This pack stops at the soundtrack and its evidence; it does not create, edit, synchronize, mux, publish, or deploy the media it may accompany.
- Use when:
  - A project needs an original instrumental soundtrack, ambient bed, theme, title cue, menu cue, or short musical piece that can be authored and revised as Strudel code.
  - The desired duration, listening context, emotional direction, and important references are known or can be clarified before composition.
  - A human is available to listen to the exported audio and decide whether the music actually fits.
  - Editable source, a reproducible official-runtime render, and a clean WAV master matter alongside the music itself.
- Not for:
  - Finding, licensing, downloading, or editing an existing commercial or royalty-free track.
  - Voiceover, dialogue, lyrics, singing, speech synthesis, podcast production, or audio restoration.
  - A video, animation, presentation, game, or website build; those are independent outcomes even when they later use this soundtrack.
  - Frame-by-frame scoring, beat synchronization, sound-effect design, muxing, publishing, or deployment unless a different outcome explicitly requests it.
  - Imitating a living artist, copying a protected melody, or treating a named reference as permission to reproduce its composition.
  - Replacing the locally cloned official Strudel application with strudel.cc, a custom partial renderer, simplified synthesizer, or hand-written approximation for the accepted export.
- Required expectations:
  - The soundtrack has a clear intended listener and use, duration, emotional direction, energy arc, reference qualities, constraints, and material to avoid before composition is judged. Evidence: musical brief; reference-quality notes; arc sketch
  - The exported soundtrack forms one deliberate musical whole appropriate to the brief, with an opening, development, meaningful contrast or progression, and an intentional loop or resolution rather than an accidental repeated sketch. Evidence: complete source; section map; full-duration audio; listening review
  - A listener can recognize a coherent motif, harmonic world, instrumental palette, and emotional identity, with each audible layer serving the piece rather than filling space. Evidence: motif and palette notes; source review; human listening review
  - The complete source plays and exports without runtime errors through a local clone of the official Codeberg Strudel repository at reviewed revision ebc25467c0f117a7e7b9b11378e21cac94d730fd, with the untouched local official export preserved. Evidence: local clone origin and reviewed commit; locked dependency install and local launch record; error-free playback or export log; untouched official WAV; source revision
  - The delivered master has the intended duration, channels, sample rate, audible continuity, headroom, dynamic behavior, and clean start and ending, with no clipping, unintended silence, missing layer, or undisclosed processing. Evidence: audio probe; loudness and peak report; section measurements; official-to-master processing record; listening review
  - A human reviewer has listened to the actual final master and explicitly accepts its musical quality and fit for the intended use; parsing, rendering, waveforms, and audio metrics alone cannot pass this expectation. Evidence: final-master listening record; reviewer decision; revision notes where needed
  - Another agent or musician can identify the final source, official export, listening master, preview, runtime provenance, processing, review decision, and limitations without reconstructing the session. Evidence: editable source; official export; selected master; handoff index; provenance and limitations
- Outputs:
  - Musical brief with intended listener and use, duration, mood, reference qualities, emotional arc, constraints, and material to avoid
  - Editable Strudel source for the complete composition
  - Untouched WAV exported by the official Strudel application
  - Listening master plus a compact preview when useful
  - Runtime, duration, channel, sample-rate, clipping, loudness, dynamic-range, and provenance record
  - Human listening review with accepted qualities, requested repairs, final decision, and remaining limitations
- Reviewed Skills:
  - Strudel Compose — Turn the approved musical direction into a coherent Strudel composition and coordinate the complete music-making workflow; source vanities/toaster-strudel; reviewed revision `1b53c590b1d84e9eff2904cdd29dae1e719c7014`
  - Strudel Emotion — Define the feeling, tension, release, contrast, restraint, and earned payoff the listener should experience; source vanities/toaster-strudel; reviewed revision `1b53c590b1d84e9eff2904cdd29dae1e719c7014`
  - Strudel Arrangement — Build a complete musical form with purposeful sections, contrast, progression, payoff, and resolution; source vanities/toaster-strudel; reviewed revision `1b53c590b1d84e9eff2904cdd29dae1e719c7014`
  - Strudel Melody — Create and develop a memorable motif with deliberate contour, rhythm, repetition, variation, and resolution; source vanities/toaster-strudel; reviewed revision `1b53c590b1d84e9eff2904cdd29dae1e719c7014`
  - Strudel Sound Design — Shape a coherent, expressive instrumental palette with movement, depth, and appropriate synthesis; source vanities/toaster-strudel; reviewed revision `1b53c590b1d84e9eff2904cdd29dae1e719c7014`
  - Strudel Mixing — Keep the full composition clear, balanced, dynamic, unclipped, and listenable across its frequency range; source vanities/toaster-strudel; reviewed revision `1b53c590b1d84e9eff2904cdd29dae1e719c7014`
  - Strudel Test — Run the source in official Strudel, expose runtime failures, export the actual audio, measure technical defects, and preserve human listening as the final judgment; source vanities/toaster-strudel; reviewed revision `1b53c590b1d84e9eff2904cdd29dae1e719c7014`
- Install:

```bash
npx skills@1.5.19 add vanities/toaster-strudel@1b53c590b1d84e9eff2904cdd29dae1e719c7014 --full-depth --skill strudel-compose --skill strudel-emotion --skill strudel-arrangement --skill strudel-melody --skill strudel-sound-design --skill strudel-mixing --skill strudel-test --agent codex
```

## Website Reference Reconstruction

- Identity: `fraylabs/possible/website-reference-reconstruction`
- Slug: `website-reference-reconstruction`
- Status: `experimental`
- Pack version: `1.0.0`
- Public page: https://possible.sh/packs/website-reference-reconstruction/
- Origin: `bundled`
- Source: package:@possible/packs
- Revision: `pack:1.0.0`
- Manifest path: `manifests/website-reference-reconstruction.json`
- Content hash: `sha256:8f7d8ce543d0851f8947d2cea8231cb7ba90398d04ec46f00c22117a81c87e7f`
- Accepted snapshot: `manifests/website-reference-reconstruction.json`
- Accepted evidence: none
- Promise: Turn a public reference website into a faithful, maintainable local reconstruction with visual and motion proof.
- Summary: A reference-first reconstruction of a public website in the target repository's existing stack. The agent captures the real page, extracts its visible system, rebuilds the static composition before its motion, compares matched reference and local states, and repairs differences before any product adaptation begins.
- Use when:
  - A public or otherwise authorized reference website should be studied closely and reconstructed in a local web project.
  - The result must preserve more than a screenshot: layout, hierarchy, responsive behavior, interaction states, timing, geometry, and motion character matter.
  - The target repository and intended reconstruction scope are known, fidelity can be reviewed against the live reference, and adaptation can wait until the reconstruction is accepted.
- Not for:
  - Copying a site's brand identity, trademarks, proprietary content, licensed assets, private source, customer data, analytics, authentication, or backend behavior.
  - Bypassing access controls, anti-bot measures, paywalls, or other technical restrictions to inspect a reference.
  - A loose mood-board exercise, an original design with no fidelity target, or a static screenshot when the reference's behavior is material.
  - Deploying, publishing, replacing a live site, or presenting the reconstruction as affiliated with the reference owner without separate approval.
- Required expectations:
  - The reconstruction begins from direct, repeatable observation of the authorized reference at named URLs, viewports, scroll positions, interaction states, and timestamps. Its layout, layers, typography, responsive transformations, interactions, and motion are represented as an explicit model rather than inferred from one screenshot or a general impression. Evidence: Reference URL and observation conditions; Full-page and fold-level desktop and mobile reference captures; Layer, state, timing, easing, path, and geometry inventory
  - The reference is reconstructed and reviewed as itself before its layout, content, colors, imagery, or behavior are adapted to the target product, so fidelity problems cannot be disguised as creative interpretation. Evidence: Accepted reference reconstruction checkpoint; Separate list of post-acceptance adaptations; Before-adaptation reference-versus-local comparison
  - The local implementation reproduces the reference's essential composition, width system, spacing rhythm, responsive behavior, interactions, and motion character in the target repository's existing architecture without becoming a brittle screenshot trace or a runtime dependency on the reference site. Evidence: Integrated source implementation; Design-token and component mapping; Behavior and motion implementation notes
  - Reference and local captures are compared at matched viewports, states, interactions, and meaningful moments in each animation cycle, and every material mismatch is either repaired or recorded as a deliberate deviation. Evidence: Matched reference and local capture set; Frame or state comparison; Deviation and repair log
  - The reconstruction remains coherent at declared desktop and mobile profiles, handles resize and content overflow, respects reduced-motion preferences, exposes usable interactive controls, and runs without material console, network, or performance failures. Evidence: Responsive browser walkthrough; Reduced-motion and interaction results; Console, network, and performance notes
  - The handoff distinguishes observed behavior and independently authored implementation from copied material, records the source and rights of every retained external asset, and does not imply affiliation with the reference owner. Evidence: Reference and asset provenance ledger; Copied-versus-reimplemented disclosure; Brand and affiliation review
- Outputs:
  - Reference observation dossier with matched desktop and mobile captures
  - Layout, typography, layer, interaction, timing, easing, and geometry model
  - Accepted still-state reconstruction checkpoint before motion
  - Responsive and maintainable local website reconstruction
  - Reconstructed interaction and motion systems
  - Reference-versus-local frame and state comparisons
  - Asset provenance and copied-versus-reimplemented disclosure
  - Deviation and repair log
  - Machine-readable website reconstruction receipt
  - Completion report with passed, failed, skipped, and unproven claims
- Reviewed Skills:
  - Webapp Testing — Repeatable browser operation, matched captures, interaction replay, and independent runtime verification; source anthropics/skills; reviewed revision `fa0fa64bdc967915dc8399e803be67759e1e62b8`
- Install:

```bash
npx skills@1.5.19 add anthropics/skills@fa0fa64bdc967915dc8399e803be67759e1e62b8 --skill webapp-testing --agent codex
```

## Cast-Driven Product Story Animation

- Identity: `fraylabs/possible/cast-driven-product-story-animation`
- Slug: `cast-driven-product-story-animation`
- Status: `experimental`
- Pack version: `1.0.0`
- Public page: https://possible.sh/packs/cast-driven-product-story-animation/
- Origin: `bundled`
- Source: package:@possible/packs

- Manifest path: `manifests/cast-driven-product-story-animation.json`
- Content hash: `sha256:e272c35d588341d0b0218eb2e814e92432acd4e4280e142e255dc4a2a307622d`
- Accepted snapshot: `manifests/cast-driven-product-story-animation.json`
- Accepted evidence: none
- Promise: Turn one product claim or real-world inspiration into a compact cast-driven website animation that makes its value understandable in a single loop.
- Summary: A story-first contract for an embedded website animation in which a distinct cast encounters an objective, coordinates through the product, produces visible progress, and reaches a readable payoff. The run separates supported fact from dramatization, creates an original and reusable character system, choreographs one causal sequence rather than decorative activity, integrates it into the existing site, and stops after responsive, reduced-motion, runtime, and comprehension proof—not deployment.
- Use when:
  - An abstract product promise becomes easier to understand when viewers can watch identifiable actors use the product to accomplish something.
  - A real event, customer story, research finding, or fictional scenario can supply a truthful narrative premise without requiring a long explanatory essay.
  - The website needs a compact looping product moment with an objective, cast, escalating action, convergence, and payoff rather than ambient particles or a generic dashboard demo.
  - Original character portraits, role continuity, responsive choreography, and a meaningful reduced-motion state can be integrated into the target repository's existing frontend stack.
- Not for:
  - A full launch film or exported video whose primary deliverable is media rather than an embedded website experience; use HTML/CSS Animated Product Launch Film or Product Launch Video.
  - A faithful recreation of another website's design or animation; use Website Reference Reconstruction before any product adaptation.
  - Decorative motion with no causal product story, a generic feature carousel, a screenshot montage, or a conventional dashboard walkthrough.
  - Reenacting uncertain allegations as fact, teaching operational wrongdoing, copying protected characters or franchise designs, or using a real person's likeness without rights.
  - Deploying, publishing, changing production configuration, or making external claims without separate approval.
- Required expectations:
  - The animation clearly distinguishes verified source facts, reasonable interpretation, fictional compression, and the product claim it is making, so dramatic energy does not turn an illustrative sequence into false evidence. Evidence: Source dossier; Dramatization and claim boundary; Final copy review
  - One complete loop visibly connects objective, cast assembly, distinct contributions, shared-state change, convergence, outcome, and product conclusion without relying on surrounding explanatory prose. Evidence: Beat table; Complete-loop review; Representative phase captures
  - Every recurring character is visually distinguishable at delivered size, has a stable name and role, and makes at least one contribution that advances the shared objective. Evidence: Character sheet and portrait map; Role-to-action matrix; Delivered-size portrait review
  - The product surface visibly carries information, state, decisions, or handoffs that enable the cast to reach the outcome; it is not merely a branded container for an unrelated story. Evidence: Product-state transition map; Before-and-after product frames; Causal product-role review
  - The loop varies pace deliberately: setup is quickly legible, contributions overlap without becoming noise, convergence creates contrast, and the outcome and conclusion each hold long enough to read before a gentle reset. Evidence: Timing map; Full-speed loop review; Mid-action, climax, conclusion, and reset captures
  - The objective, characters, product action, outcome, and conclusion remain coherent at declared desktop and mobile profiles and in the reduced-motion state. Evidence: Desktop and mobile walkthrough; Reduced-motion capture; Resize, zoom, and overflow notes
  - Character art, icons, fonts, and retained visual assets are original or licensed, their prompts and sources are recorded, and their design does not imitate a protected franchise or real person's likeness. Evidence: Asset ledger; Generation prompts or license links; Originality and likeness review
  - The animation is reviewed inside the actual page, loads locally from declared assets, completes and resets consistently, and passes the target repository's relevant checks without material console, layout, or performance failures. Evidence: Integrated page walkthrough; Runtime and console report; Repository check results
- Outputs:
  - Source dossier with verified facts, dramatization boundary, citations, and supported product claim
  - One-sentence visitor conclusion and causal phase table
  - Original cast brief, cohesive character sheet, portrait mapping, prompts, and asset ledger
  - Responsive website animation integrated into the target product surface
  - Deterministic timing map covering objective, assembly, action, convergence, payoff, conclusion, and reset
  - Meaningful reduced-motion state
  - Representative desktop and mobile phase captures
  - Fresh-viewer comprehension and runtime report
  - Machine-readable outcome receipt with passed, failed, skipped, and unproven checks
- Reviewed Skills:
  - HyperFrames — Design the causal beat structure, character-led visual system, readable phase choreography, and deterministic motion review; source heygen-com/hyperframes; reviewed revision `b08cefea631b2c13697b6cb31075bf5a9b7c738d`
  - Webapp Testing — Independently verify the integrated loop, representative phases, responsive states, accessibility fallback, and runtime behavior; source anthropics/skills; reviewed revision `fa0fa64bdc967915dc8399e803be67759e1e62b8`
- Install:

```bash
npx skills@1.5.19 add heygen-com/hyperframes@b08cefea631b2c13697b6cb31075bf5a9b7c738d --full-depth --skill hyperframes --agent codex
npx skills@1.5.19 add anthropics/skills@fa0fa64bdc967915dc8399e803be67759e1e62b8 --skill webapp-testing --agent codex
```
